To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency of stenosis of the MHA in men of the age group 40-65 years is high (20%) and increases with age.
the frequency of stenoses of the major arteries in the head is high in men aged 40-70 years, and is related to the age and severity of vascular disease.
the prevalence of MHA stenos is high in the population of middle-aged men and increases with age and the degree of vascular involvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the high frequency of MHA involvement in atherosclerosis, the high frequency of hemodynamic changes and the necessity of their early diagnosis.
the frequency and severity of MHA steno-occlusive disease and its relation to the age, sex and the presence of vascular involvement.
the frequency of hemodynamic changes and stenosis of MHA in subjects with clinically normal and abnormal vessels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atherosclerosis is a multifactorial disease.
atherosclerotic lesions of MHA are common in the population and that they are associated with vascular diseases.
MHA stenoses were more frequent in subjects with vascular involvement than in controls and the stenoses were related to the severity of the vascular involvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of MHA involvement with atherosclerosis is very high in males.
atherosclerosis of MHA is a common disease in the population of the examined age group.
the ultrasonic dopplerographic study of MHA in a population of males aged over 40 is a reliable method to detect early stages of atherosclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atherosclerosis of MHA is a common disease and is often asymptomatic.

a significant proportion of patients with vascular diseases and even healthy individuals have hemodynamically significant lesions of the major head arteries, which is a potential source of cerebrovascular events.
atherosclerosis in MHA is a frequent and severe disease in the examined age group.
